answer: In a market for glacier surveys, canyon maps and ledge inspections, each active agent identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. The same funds cannot back multiple identities, so an attacker running 1,000 fake agents must immobilize $100,000 for the month. This does not prove that agents have different owners; it makes a swarm costly by tying its size to committed capital instead of freely generated usernames.
